mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi engine typically costs between £2,500 and £4,000 for supply only, while used units start from around £500.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs of Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi engine failure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Owners of the Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi should watch for persistent limp mode, excessive black smoke from the exhaust, and a noticeable loss of power under acceleration.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Given that Mk4 and early Mk5 Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi models typically hold a market value between £1,500 and £6,000, a full rebuilt engine can cost more than the car is worth.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard supply-only delivery of a Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi engine takes 1 to 3 working days via nationwide courier.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the QXWA and TXWA engine codes in the Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The QXWA code was used in the standard Mondeo (2007-2015) and produces 160PS, while the TXWA code was introduced for the Titanium X and Sport trims with an increased output of 200PS.

historyTimeline.h2: Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched as the robust, high-torque diesel workhorse in the Mondeo range, the 2.2 TDCi variant spanned the Mk4 generation and early Mk5 models, offering strong motorway refinement and towing capability before being phased out in favour of the more efficient 2.0 TDCi unit.

milestones.description: QXWA / UFWA, 2.2L Diesel, 140-160PS (103-118kW) - Introduced in the Mk4 Mondeo, providing a reliable and powerful diesel option for Zetec and Titanium trims.
TXWA, 2.2L Diesel, 200PS (147kW) - High-output variant introduced for the Mondeo Titanium X and Sport trims, featuring a larger turbocharger and revised injection mapping.
QXWB / TXWB, 2.2L Diesel, 160-200PS - Early Mk5 Mondeo carryover, featuring minor emissions and EGR refinements to meet Euro 5 standards before the transition to the 2.0 TDCi.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi is generally a robust Duratorq unit, but high-mileage examples are prone to specific wear points. The QXWA, TXWA, and UFWA codes dominate replacement demand for this variant due to DPF, turbo, and injector-related failures. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF Clogging & EGR Failure - Why the Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi (QXWA/UFWA) Restricts Airflow
problems.rootCause: Short urban journeys prevent the DPF from completing active regeneration cycles, while exhaust gases recirculated by the EGR valve deposit heavy carbon soot, restricting airflow and triggering limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical DPF clean and EGR maintenance.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for early-stage clogging, but does not fix underlying mechanical wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call when carbon damage has caused secondary issues like turbo starvation or severe compression loss.

problems.recommendation: For most Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi owners, a targeted component repair (DPF clean, EGR service, or turbo refurbishment) offers the best financial return if the engine block is fundamentally sound. However, if the engine has suffered catastrophic turbo debris ingestion or severe internal wear, sourcing a low-mileage used engine is often the most economically viable path, provided it comes with a verifiable warranty.

problems.h4: Turbocharger & Injector Failure - Why the Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi (TXWA) Loses Power
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger actuator linkage wears or seizes due to heat cycling, while aging injectors can develop leak-off issues, creating rough idling and loss of power.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removing the turbo for refurbishment and servicing/replacing injectors.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if the engine block and compression remain healthy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if turbo failure has sent debris into the engine or if compression is compromised.

items.question: What are the common signs of Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi engine failure?
items.answer: Owners of the Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi should watch for persistent limp mode, excessive black smoke from the exhaust, and a noticeable loss of power under acceleration.
keyPoints: A rough idle or misfire often indicates failing injectors or severe DPF clogging.
If the engine management light is flashing alongside these symptoms, stop driving immediately.
Continuing to drive can cause catastrophic internal damage to the turbocharger or engine block.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi?
items.answer: Given that Mk4 and early Mk5 Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi models typically hold a market value between £1,500 and £6,000, a full rebuilt engine can cost more than the car is worth.
keyPoints: For most owners, sourcing a verified low-mileage used engine is the most financially sensible option.
Investing in targeted component repairs (like a DPF clean or turbo refurbishment) is also viable if the engine block is healthy.
A rebuilt unit is only recommended if you plan to keep the vehicle long-term and it holds exceptional condition.

items.question: What is the difference between the QXWA and TXWA engine codes in the Ford Mondeo 2.2 TDCi?
items.answer: The QXWA code was used in the standard Mondeo (2007-2015) and produces 160PS, while the TXWA code was introduced for the Titanium X and Sport trims with an increased output of 200PS.
keyPoints: Although they share the same 2.2L Duratorq architecture, their turbocharger setups and ECU mappings differ significantly.
Swapping them requires careful verification of compatibility, especially regarding the turbo and intercooler piping.
Always verify your exact engine code via your V5C logbook or registration before ordering a replacement.
